directAnswer: You can share your phone's internet connection by enabling the hotspot feature in your device's settings.
summary: This guide provides steps to share your smartphone's internet connection via Wi-Fi hotspot, Bluetooth, or USB tethering.

sections.heading: Using Wi-Fi Hotspot
sections.body: Most smartphones allow you to create a Wi-Fi hotspot, enabling other devices to connect to your phone's internet.

sections.heading: Using Bluetooth Tethering
sections.body: You can also share your internet connection via Bluetooth, which is useful for connecting devices without Wi-Fi capabilities.

sections.heading: Using USB Tethering
sections.body: USB tethering allows you to connect your phone to a computer using a USB cable, sharing your internet connection directly.

steps.title: Enable Wi-Fi Hotspot on Android
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering > Wi-Fi hotspot, then toggle it on.

steps.title: Enable Wi-Fi Hotspot on iPhone
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Personal Hotspot, then toggle 'Allow Others to Join' on.

steps.title: Enable Bluetooth Tethering
steps.detail: On Android, go to Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering > Bluetooth tethering. On iPhone, enable Bluetooth in Settings > Bluetooth.

steps.title: Enable USB Tethering
steps.detail: Connect your phone to a computer with a USB cable. On Android, go to Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering > USB tethering. On iPhone, it usually activates automatically.

faqs.question: Will sharing my internet connection drain my battery?
faqs.answer: Yes, using your phone as a hotspot can significantly drain the battery, so it's advisable to keep it plugged in if possible.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to how many devices can connect?
faqs.answer: Yes, most smartphones have a limit on the number of devices that can connect to the hotspot, typically ranging from 5 to 10 devices.

faqs.question: Can I share my internet connection while on a call?
faqs.answer: This depends on your carrier and device. Some carriers allow sharing while on a call, while others may not.

caveats: Data charges may apply depending on your mobile plan.
